newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Swimming-Australia, China dominate World Cup meeting.
newsitem.headline: Swimming-Australia, China dominate World Cup meeting.

text.p: The young Australian men's squad and the teenaged Chinese women fired warnings to the swimming world with powerful performances in the first leg of the World Cup short course series on Sunday.
The Australians finished the two-day meeting with nine gold medals while the Chinese women collected seven.
Nineteen-year-old Michael Klim led the Australian assault on the second day by adding gold medals in the 200 metres freestyle and the 100 metres butterfly to the two titles he won on Saturday.

He was joined in the winner's enclosure by Adrian Radley, who added the 50 metres backstroke and 200 metres backstroke titles to the 100 metres backstroke he lifted on Saturday, and Matthew Dunn, who took the 200 metres individual medley for his second gold.

"It is about time Australia really became a force in international swimming," said Klim, who trains at the Australian Institute of Sport. "A lot of young guys are coming through and I think you will be hearing a lot about them."
Klim trains alongside the great Russian Alexander Popov whom he said was inspiring him to greater heights ahead of the 2000 Sydney Olympics.

"He is someone with a mission and that is what I am striving for as well," he said. "Winning a gold medal in front of home fans at the Sydney Olympics (in 2000) would be great but there are a lot of steps to be taken before then. My first goal is the world championships in Perth next January and then I will focus on the Olympics."

China's women added three gold medals to their four from the first day. Seventeen-year-old Chen Yan swept to victory in the 100 metres backstroke for her second gold and 15-year-olds Wang Wei and Nian Yun also tasted double delight by winning the 200 metres breaststroke and 100 metres freestyle respectively.

Nian was particularly impressive as she beat Atlanta Olympic gold medallist Claudia Poll by .34 seconds. But the Costa Rican bounced back to take the 400 metres freestyle ahead of China's Wang Luna for her third gold of the weekend.

"The World Cup season is great for our younger swimmers. They are sharp at the moment and they have risen to the challenge of racing Olympians and other international calibre swimmers," said China's deputy head coach, Zhang Xiong.
"Many of our Olympians have taken time off but they will be competing in future legs - they may be a bit slower to get back to form."

Poll said she was happy with her times following a five-month break from competitive swimming. "I took time off after the Atlanta Olympics so to come back and win three gold medals and a silver in good times is pretty satisfying," she said.
